subtitle: 5 questions in real GMAT format. A new quiz on this week's words goes live every Sunday.
instructions: You have 45 seconds per question; the quiz moves on when time runs out.
Your score appears the moment you finish.

questions.prompt: The venture capital board dismissed the founder's valuation model as ________, pointing out that it relied on an unproven hypothesis that user acquisition costs would decline to zero within six months.
questions.explanation: 'Fallacious' means based on a mistaken belief or unsound reasoning. Since the model relied on an unproven and implausible hypothesis, describing it as 'fallacious' correctly captures the logical vulnerability in the argument.

questions.prompt: The legal counsel argued that the supplier had given ________ approval to the contract modifications, as they had accepted payments under the new tariff schedule without objection for three consecutive quarters.
questions.explanation: 'Tacit' means understood or implied without being stated directly. Accepting modified terms and payments over three quarters without protest represents implied or tacit agreement.

questions.prompt: Rather than relying on abstract corporate dogma, the interim chief executive adopted a resolutely ________ approach, restructuring division budgets based solely on verifiable operating margins.
questions.explanation: 'Pragmatic' means dealing with situations realistically and practically based on real-world outcomes rather than theoretical dogma, which directly matches basing decisions on 'verifiable operating margins'.

questions.prompt: To ________ their claim that regional consumer confidence had rebounded, market analysts presented third-quarter retail data demonstrating an 18% increase in discretionary household spending.
questions.explanation: 'Substantiate' means to provide evidence to support or prove the truth of a claim. Discretionary spending data was used to substantiate (support) the analysts' thesis.

questions.prompt: The auditor noted that the executive's statements were deliberately ________, using evasive language that could be interpreted either as a denial of wrongdoing or as an admission of regulatory negligence.
questions.explanation: 'Equivocal' means open to more than one interpretation or deliberately ambiguous, matching the auditor's observation of language that could be read in two contradictory ways.
